hooks.name: Physics Safety Gate
hooks.description: Gates write operations to physics-critical source files, enforcing coordinate conventions, unit consistency, covariance integrity, and formula provenance before changes are applied.

action.prompt:
Before writing to any file matching src/orbital_mechanics.py, src/conjunction.py, or src/damage_minimization.py, enforce these physics integrity rules:

1. COORDINATE CONVENTION: All position vectors must remain in ECI (Earth-Centered Inertial) frame. If the change introduces a different frame (RTN, LVLH, perifocal), it must include an explicit conversion back to ECI at the function boundary.

2. UNITS: All internal calculations must use SI units (meters, seconds, kg) or the project's documented km/km·s⁻¹ convention as established in src/utils.py. Never mix unit systems within a single function. Any new constant must reference its source and units in a comment.

3. COVARIANCE INTEGRITY: Any code that constructs or modifies a covariance matrix must preserve symmetry (C = Cᵀ) and positive semi-definiteness. If eigenvalues are computed, they must be clamped to ≥ 1e-10 to prevent numerical singularity.

4. FORMULA PROVENANCE: If the change modifies or introduces a physics formula (force model, probability calculation, coordinate transform), require a comment citing the source — either a reference to docs/physics.md, a publication, or a standard (e.g., "NASA Standard Breakup Model", "Alfriend/Akella method").

5. CONSERVATION LAWS: Changes to propagation or force evaluation must not violate energy conservation in the unperturbed (two-body) case. If perturbations are added, document the expected energy drift rate.

If any of these rules would be violated by the proposed write, flag the concern with permissionDecision "ask" so the user can review before proceeding.
